name: Xor Filters: Faster and Smaller Than Bloom and Cuckoo Filters (Graf & Lemire, JEA 2020)
workload: Random 64-bit key membership queries and filter construction time, xor filter vs. Bloom, blocked Bloom, and cuckoo filter implementations at comparable false-positive rates
claimed_speedup: Xor filters query faster and use less memory than Bloom and cuckoo filters at equivalent false-positive rates (exact per-configuration multipliers are in the paper's benchmark tables, not restated here)
stars_or_usage: 432 stars (fastfilter/xor_singleheader); paper published in ACM Journal of Experimental Algorithmics 25(1), 2020, DOI 10.1145/3376122
tradeoffs: Xor filters are immutable/static (no insertion or deletion after construction), unlike Bloom/cuckoo filters
caveats: fastfilter/xor_singleheader and fastfilter/xorfilter are already in the known-catalogue list; this entry records a peer-reviewed (Tier B) benchmark source surfaced via Hacker News (thread id 21840821, 457 points, and dl.acm.org thread id 22742905, 95 points) per the is_evidence_for_known exception. Could not access the ACM DL page directly (Cloudflare-blocked) or the arXiv PDF's exact hardware/compiler table this session, so those fields are left null rather than guessed.
found_via: Hacker News: query "xor filter" -> https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=21840821 (Lemire blog) and https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=22742905 (ACM DL paper)

name: Binary Fuse Filters: Fast and Smaller Than Xor Filters (Graf & Lemire, JEA 2022)
baseline: Bloom filter, cuckoo filter, xor filter
workload: Static-set membership filters compared for storage overhead and query/construction speed against Bloom filters, blocked Bloom filters, vector quotient filters, cuckoo filters, xor filters, and ribbon filters
claimed_speedup: Binary fuse filters are within 13% (8% at reduced query speed) of the information-theoretic storage lower bound vs. 23% for xor filters and 44% for Bloom filters, and filter construction can be more than 2x faster than xor filter construction, without sacrificing query speed
stars_or_usage: 432 stars (fastfilter/xor_singleheader); paper published in ACM Journal of Experimental Algorithmics 27, 2022, DOI 10.1145/3510449
tradeoffs: Static/immutable filter like xor filters; construction requires the full key set up front
caveats: fastfilter/xor_singleheader is already in the known-catalogue list; this records a peer-reviewed (Tier B) benchmark surfaced via Hacker News (thread id 46658128, 138 points) per the is_evidence_for_known exception. Exact hardware/CPU model and compiler flags from the paper were not independently re-verified this session (ACM DL fetch was Cloudflare-blocked), so left null.

name: cfilter (Cuckoo Filter implementation in Go)
workload: No benchmark numbers published; README and Show HN title assert general superiority over Bloom filters for approximate set-membership queries (lower space overhead, deletion support, higher performance) but provide no measured figures
claimed_speedup: Unquantified claim: "Better Than Bloom Filters" / "achieving even higher performance than Bloom filters"
stars_or_usage: 751 stars; Show HN front-page thread with 181 points; cited as a reference implementation by seiflotfy/cuckoofilter
tradeoffs: Supports deletion (unlike a plain Bloom filter) at the cost of a small chance of deleting the wrong item on fingerprint collision
caveats: No numbers anywhere in the repo or the linked HN discussion; included as the run's single allowed Tier D entry given notability (HN front page, 751 stars, cross-referenced by other cuckoo filter implementations). Language is Go, not C++, so this only qualifies under the "then any" fallback, not the C++-first preference.
found_via: Hacker News: Show HN thread https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=12241332 ("Show HN: Cuckoo Filter Implementation in Go, Better Than Bloom Filters")
